summary: Richard Sproat works in computational linguistics. He studied at the University of California, San Diego and MIT, and later held positions at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2003–2009), Oregon Health and Science University (2009–2012), and Google (2012).

Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1953–1958) and Princeton University (~1958–1963). He held academic posts at the University of Sydney (~1963–1964) and the Australian National University, where he became a fellow in 1971.

Richard Taupier works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate and MS at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he served as Associate Director of Research Development, and lectured at Smith College.

Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied at the University of Iowa and completed his doctorate under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania. He served as dean at UT Austin, provost at KU, and president of the University of Oregon and Field Museum.

Richard Wilhelm was a sinologist educated at the Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen (~1891–1895). He served as a guest professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924, which he founded in 1925.

Richard von Garbe was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen and Königsberg under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Grassmann, and Bhagavata Acharya. He held professorships at the University of Königsberg (1878–1880, 1894) and the University of Tübingen (1895–1927).

Richard von Glahn works in sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and served as a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He pursued his studies under teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Rigzin Lhundup worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1959 and 1987.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who conducted her doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki. Her supervisors and teachers included Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, Hannu Riikonen, and Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rikizan Ishikawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who was educated at Komazawa University. He later served there as Professor of Buddhist Studies from approximately 1990 to 1997.

Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru, and founded Bodhicharya.
Rinzin Thargyal worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo by 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004 under Lambert Schmithausen), and held posts at the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from UW–Milwaukee and the University of Chicago. She served at the American Academy of Religion (1974) and was a professor at UW–Eau Claire (~1979–1998).

Rizong Sras Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. After monastic training at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1959) studying under the 14th Dalai Lama, Losal Ling Khen Zur Jampal Sampel, and Pema Gyaltsen, he served as abbot of Gyume, Samstanling, and Drepung Loseling.

Rob Linrothe specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and art history. He studied at the University of Minnesota, the Inter-University Program, and the University of Chicago (PhD), and held posts at the National Palace Museum, Rubin Museum, Skidmore College, and Northwestern University.

Rob Nairn was a Buddhist studies scholar with legal and criminological degrees from the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, and the University of Edinburgh. He held professorial posts at Zimbabwe and Cape Town, and studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and 16th Karmapa.

Robert A. F. Thurman was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Geshe Wangyal, the 14th Dalai Lama, and others. He founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies and held posts at Amherst College (1973–1988) and Columbia University (1988–2019).
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under doctoral supervisor Patrick Olivelle.
